---
title: "Fit a BayesA Marker-Specific Variance Model (MCMC or stochastic EM)"
---

## Fit a BayesA Marker-Specific Variance Model (MCMC or stochastic EM) {.unnumbered}


### Description

BayesA (Meuwissen et al., 2001) places a scaled inverse chi-squared
prior on each allele's effect variance, allowing heavier-tailed
effect-size distributions than ridge regression. Use <code>method =
"mcmc"</code> for full posterior inference or <code>method = "em"</code> for fast
stochastic-EM point estimates (Gaussian only).



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>run_bayesa(
  w,
  y,
  wtw_diag,
  X = NULL,
  nu = 4.5,
  sigma2_g,
  sigma2_e_init,
  prior_params = NULL,
  mcmc_params = NULL,
  em_params = NULL,
  method = c("mcmc", "em"),
  response_type = c("gaussian", "binary"),
  fold_id = 0L,
  save_rds = FALSE,
  save_path = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="w">w</code></td>
<td>
Numeric design matrix (<code>n x p</code>). Typically the
<code>\$W_ah</code> element returned by <code>construct_wah_matrix</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="y">y</code></td>
<td>
Phenotype vector (length <code>n</code>). Use 0/1 for binary traits.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="wtw_diag">wtw_diag</code></td>
<td>
Pre-computed <code>colSums(w^2)</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="X">X</code></td>
<td>
Optional fixed-effects design matrix (<code>n x q</code>). When
supplied, the model is $y = X\alpha + W\beta + \mu + \epsilon$
with a flat prior on $\alpha$. Do <strong>not</strong> include a column
of ones for the intercept; $\mu$ is sampled separately.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="nu">nu</code></td>
<td>
Degrees of freedom for the scaled inverse chi-squared prior on
marker variances. Smaller values allow heavier tails. Must be &gt; 2.
Default <code>4.5</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="sigma2_g">sigma2_g</code></td>
<td>
Prior total genetic variance. Typically
<code>var(y) * 0.5</code>; for binary traits use <code>1.0</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="sigma2_e_init">sigma2_e_init</code></td>
<td>
Initial residual variance. For binary traits fix
at <code>1.0</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="prior_params">prior_params</code></td>
<td>
Optional named list. Only <code>a0_e</code> (default 10)
is used; <code>b0_e</code> is derived as <code>sigma2_e_init * (a0_e - 1)</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="mcmc_params">mcmc_params</code></td>
<td>
Optional named list: <code>n_iter</code> (40000),
<code>n_burn</code> (20000), <code>n_thin</code> (10), <code>seed</code> (123).
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="em_params">em_params</code></td>
<td>
Optional named list: <code>max_iter</code> (500), <code>tol</code>
(<code>1e-6</code>).
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="method">method</code></td>
<td>
Either <code>"mcmc"</code> (default) or <code>"em"</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="response_type">response_type</code></td>
<td>
<code>"gaussian"</code> (default) or <code>"binary"</code>.
Binary requires <code>method = "mcmc"</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="fold_id">fold_id</code></td>
<td>
Integer label for progress messages.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="save_rds">save_rds</code></td>
<td>
If <code>TRUE</code>, the fit object is saved to
disk as an RDS file. Set <code>FALSE</code> (default) for CV loops.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="save_path">save_path</code></td>
<td>
Optional explicit RDS path. If <code>NULL</code> (default),
defaults to <code>"results_bayesa.Rds"</code> in the current working
directory.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="verbose">verbose</code></td>
<td>
If <code>TRUE</code>, the Rust engine streams per-iteration
progress (start banner, Iter X/Y diagnostics, ESS / Geweke,
completion) to stderr. Default <code>FALSE</code> keeps the Rust side
silent. The brief R post-fit summary prints regardless.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Details

<strong>Algorithm choice.</strong> MCMC uses marginalised Gibbs sampling and
returns full posterior chains. EM is much faster but provides no
uncertainty quantification and does not support <code>response_type =
"binary"</code>.

<strong>Auto-save.</strong> By default the returned fit is saved to
<code>results_bayesa.Rds</code> in <code>getwd()</code>. Set <code>save_rds = FALSE</code>
for CV loops.

<strong>Three usage scenarios.</strong> <code>run_bayesa()</code> +
<code>summary()</code> + <code>predict()</code> support full-data fits,
train-test splits, and k-fold CV uniformly. See
<code>run_bayesr</code> for example loops.

<strong>Derived parameter.</strong> The wrapper computes
<code>s_squared = sigma2_g * (nu - 2) / (nu * sum(apply(w, 2, var)))</code>
so the prior expectation of each marker variance equals
<code>sigma2_g / sum_2pq</code>.



### Value

An object of class <code>c("masbayes_bayesa", "masbayes")</code> — a
list with the following key fields:


<dl>
<dt><code>beta_hat, mu_hat, sigma2_e_hat, sigma2_j_hat</code></dt><dd>Posterior
point estimates (intercept, allele effects, residual variance,
per-marker variances).
</dd>
<dt><code>beta_samples, sigma2_j_samples, sigma2_e_samples,
    mu_samples</code></dt><dd>Posterior chains (single-row matrices for EM).
</dd>
<dt><code>GEBV / pred_train, h2, sigma2_g, sigma2_e</code></dt><dd>Training
GEBVs (liability scale for binary), heritability, and total
variance components.
</dd>
<dt><code>prob_train</code></dt><dd>Binary only: training-set predicted
probabilities <code>P(y = 1) = pnorm(pred_train)</code> (probit
inverse link from Albert-Chib augmentation).
</dd>
<dt><code>runtime</code></dt><dd>Elapsed seconds.
</dd>
<dt><code>training_metrics</code></dt><dd><code>R2</code>, <code>RMSE</code>,
<code>accuracy</code> (or <code>AUC</code> for binary), <code>bias</code>. For
binary, all metrics are on the observed (probability) scale —
<code>bias</code> is the calibration slope (1.0 = perfectly
calibrated) and <code>RMSE\^2</code> approximates the Brier score.
AUC is rank-invariant so unaffected.
</dd>
<dt><code>diagnostics</code></dt><dd>ESS / Geweke Z (MCMC only).
</dd>
<dt><code>variance_components</code></dt><dd>Per-marker variances binned into
tertiles (small / medium / large) reporting mean, range, and
marker count.
</dd>
<dt><code>rds_path</code></dt><dd>Path of the saved RDS file, or <code>NULL</code>.
</dd>
</dl>



### References

Meuwissen, T. H. E., Hayes, B. J., \&amp; Goddard, M. E. (2001).
Prediction of total genetic value using genome-wide dense marker
maps. <em>Genetics</em>, 157(4), 1819-1829.
[doi:10.1093/genetics/157.4.1819](https://doi.org/10.1093/genetics/157.4.1819)



### See Also

<code>run_bayesr</code>, <code>construct_wah_matrix</code>,
<code>summary.masbayes_bayesa</code>,
<code>predict.masbayes_bayesa</code>



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masbayes")

set.seed(42)
n     <- 200
mcmc  <- list(n_iter = 2000L, n_burn = 1000L, n_thin = 5L, seed = 123L)
X_cov <- cbind(sex = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5), batch = rnorm(n))  # optional

# ---- (A) SNP path ------------------------------------------------------
n_snp <- 100
X     <- matrix(rbinom(n * n_snp, 2, prob = runif(n_snp, 0.1, 0.5)),
                n, n_snp)
W_snp <- construct_snp_matrix(X)$W
y     <- W_snp[, 1:5] %*% rnorm(5, 0, 0.5) + rnorm(n, 0, 1)

fit_snp <- run_bayesa(
  w             = W_snp,
  y             = y,
  wtw_diag      = colSums(W_snp^2),
  X             = X_cov,           # optional
  nu            = 4.5,
  sigma2_g      = var(y) * 0.5,
  sigma2_e_init = var(y) * 0.5,
  mcmc_params   = mcmc
)
summary(fit_snp)

# ---- (B) Microhaplotype path ------------------------------------------
n_block <- 50
hap <- matrix(sample.int(3, n * n_block * 2, replace = TRUE), nrow = n)
colnames(hap) <- paste0("hap_", rep(seq_len(n_block), each = 2))
freq <- data.frame(
  haplotype = paste0("hap_", rep(seq_len(n_block), each = 3)),
  allele    = rep(1:3, n_block),
  freq      = rep(c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2), n_block)
)
W_mh <- construct_wah_matrix(hap, colnames(hap), freq)$W_ah
y_mh <- W_mh[, 1:5] %*% rnorm(5, 0, 0.5) + rnorm(n, 0, 1)

fit_mh <- run_bayesa(
  w             = W_mh,
  y             = y_mh,
  wtw_diag      = colSums(W_mh^2),
  X             = X_cov,           # optional
  nu            = 4.5,
  sigma2_g      = var(y_mh) * 0.5,
  sigma2_e_init = var(y_mh) * 0.5,
  mcmc_params   = mcmc
)
summary(fit_mh)

# ---- Predict on a held-out test set -----------------------------------
idx  <- sample(n, 0.8 * n)
W_tr <- W_snp[idx, ]
y_tr <- y[idx]
fit  <- run_bayesa(
  w             = W_tr,
  y             = y_tr,
  wtw_diag      = colSums(W_tr^2),
  nu            = 4.5,
  sigma2_g      = var(y_tr) * 0.5,
  sigma2_e_init = var(y_tr) * 0.5,
  mcmc_params   = mcmc
)
pred <- predict(fit, W_snp[-idx, ], y[-idx])
pred$metrics$accuracy




```
